# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

But within the test, `env.forcedIds = ['sh-1-aaaa']` — the `entry.id` will be 'sh-1-aaaa'. The near-miss becomes 'sh-1-aazz'. But wait — could 'sh-1-aazz' resolve to 'sh-1-aaaa' as a near-miss and then stop? Let me check the resolution logic: AC5 asserts that `stop` with a near-miss returns a hint and kills nothing. Is that the actual behavior in builtin_tools_bash.dart:906? The PR description says the refusal hint is the near-miss branch. Also, near-miss resolution on stop: does stop resolve the near-miss to the exact id and then refuse? Need to verify the code path: resolution unique same-n → ShellJobNearMiss → stop refuses. Let me check.

Also check one subtlety: the comment says "The minted id's random base36 tail ends in 'zz' once every ~36^2 starts" — correct.

Now the important checks on Family B fix:

1. `_headlessSteerDue` duplicates the crossing logic from `_steerHeadlessLiveness`. There's a subtle difference: `_steerHeadlessLiveness` checks `elapsedMs ~/ quietMs > (consumedBucket ?? 0)` — same. But `_headlessSteerDue` checks `!job.isRunning || !job.notifyOnSettle` — but `active` is already filtered by `_headlessActiveShellJobs()` which only includes running + notifyOnSettle. Minor redundancy, fine.

2. A timing consideration: `_headlessSteerDue` computes `steerDue` at round start, using `_waitingClock()` separately from `now` passed to `wakeIn`. So `now` is read twice (line 245 `final now = _waitingClock();` then again inside `_headlessSteerDue` via `_waitingClock()`). With a fake clock this could be inconsistent but both reads are close. Minor.

3. Potential issue: `remainingCeiling: deadline.difference(now)` — if the deadline has already passed, remainingCeiling is negative, `Future.delayed` with negative duration completes immediately — same spin. But then next round `_headlessDrainAction` will return detach since `!now.isBefore(deadline)`. So at most one instant round before detach; the loop breaks. Actually wait — let's check the drain loop: rounds are capped at 10; after each round, `_headlessDrainAction` decides. If deadline passed, detach. So the spin would end after one extra round. Fine.

4. The more subtle issue: when the wake is non-positive and steerDue is false, the round now sleeps `remainingCeiling` — the FULL remaining ceiling, ignoring `waits` settle futures via Future.any (still in place — Future.any still waits for both). OK.

But wait — there's a potential issue: a non-positive wake with nothing to consume could happen mid-drain when a liveness threshold... no, if a threshold is due then steerDue would be true. Consider: quietMs = 1000, job started, now elapsed 2500ms, consumedBucket=2, next threshold at 3000ms → wake = 3000-2500 = 500ms positive. Fine. Negative wake happens when elapsed > deadline-now, i.e. the deadline pulls earlier... actually wake = min over thresholds and deadline difference. If the deadline difference is negative (deadline passed), wake negative. Then steerDue may be true if a threshold crossed. If steerDue true, we take instant wake — spin of one round, then detach since deadline passed. OK.

But here's a real concern: after sleeping the remaining ceiling when steerDue is false, when we wake at deadline, `_steerHeadlessLiveness` runs, and thresholds that crossed during the sleep are steered — consumed. Good, no loss.

5. Another subtle case: `steerDue` is computed at the start of the round, but the `wakeIn` may be positive yet tiny; not an issue.

6. What about when `wake` is positive but the steer becomes due during the wait... `wakeIn` pulls earlier by next threshold, so wake fires at the threshold and steer is consumed. Good.

7. Edge: multiple jobs — `_headlessSteerDue` returns true if ANY job has a due crossing, even if `wakeIn` is dominated by another job's sooner threshold. Then instant wake → round spins once but the steer fires on cadence. Fine per design.

8. Now, `headlessDrainRoundSleep` returns `remainingCeiling` when wake <= 0 and !steerDue. But consider: the never-settling job test expects detach with 'drain ceiling'. With the fix, each round sleeps remainingCeiling (roughly the full remaining budget since wake consumed nothing...). Actually wait — after each round the clock advances by remainingCeiling, so next round remainingCeiling shrinks. After round 1: slept remaining ceiling → deadline reached → `_headlessDrainAction` → detach with 'drain ceiling'. 

But hold on: is there an issue with the first round? now ≈ deadline - drainMs, wake = min over jobs of threshold distances. If quietMs is default (what is defaultShellJobQuietMs? probably 300 or so), and drainMs is small in tests... The test at line 465 expects drain ceiling. OK.

9. There's a question about whether the spin could still happen via `steerDue` oscillation: steerDue true → instant wake → steer consumes bucket → next round steerDue false, wake: next threshold positive. So no continuous spin.

But one more: `_headlessSteerDue` uses `liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] ?? 0` and `elapsedMs ~/ quietMs > consumed`. `_steerHeadlessLiveness` skips `currentBucket <= lastBucket`. Same condition. Good.

10. Duplication: `_headlessSteerDue` duplicates the bucket-crossing logic inline rather than reusing a pure function. There's already a pure `headlessJobLivenessAction` in headless_config.dart, but its semantics differ (probed check etc.). The duplicated logic between `_headlessSteerDue` and `_steerHeadlessLiveness` is a maintainability concern — if the crossing rule changes, two places must be updated. The doc comment acknowledges "the same crossing check [_steerHeadlessLiveness] applies". This is a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT: could extract a shared `_headlessCrossedBucket` helper. I'd call it SUGGESTION given the doc-comment cross-reference.

Actually, there's a subtle divergence risk: `_headlessSteerDue` re-checks `job.isRunning` and `job.notifyOnSettle` — the same filter as the active list construction. `_steerHeadlessLiveness` also re-checks. Consistent.

11. Test coverage: pure function unit tests added — good. No integration test that exercises the actual loop with a fake clock to prevent regression of the spin. That's an IMPORTANT gap? The PR says the new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. But nothing tests that `_headlessSteerDue` is correctly wired into the round. An integration test would catch wiring mistakes (e.g., steerDue computed but ignored). Hmm — the existing drain ITs at agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart presumably exercise the loop with fake clock, and with a fake clock the wake might never be non-positive. So the wiring path is untested. I'd rate this SUGGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. Given that the fix's whole point is wiring, and a wiring error would silently keep the flake, I'd say IMPORTANT.

12. Line numbers in pr_diff: inline comment lines must exist in diff. Let me check possible findings:

a) In `agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` line ~245-253: `now` read via `_waitingClock()`, then `_headlessSteerDue` reads `_waitingClock()` again — double clock read, inconsistent under a fake clock between reads. Minor; SUGGESTION: pass `now` into `_headlessSteerDue` to keep one time base. Actually `wakeIn` uses `now` and steerDue uses a fresh read — if the clock advanced between, steerDue could see a crossing while wakeIn's deadline difference includes it... marginal. SUGGESTION.

b) Duplication of crossing logic — SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT.

c) `remainingCeiling` could be negative → negative Future.delayed completes instantly → still one spin round; bounded by next detach decision. Fine, but the pure function returns a negative duration in that case; the docstring says "a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling". Not a bug.

d) Test: `headlessDrainRoundSleep` when `wake` is positive but larger than remainingCeiling? Can wakeIn return a wake larger than remaining ceiling? wake starts at deadline.difference(now) = remainingCeiling, and only pulls earlier. So wake ≤ remainingCeiling always from wakeIn. But the pure function doesn't enforce…

Now I have a good understanding. Let me analyze the fix's correctness carefully once more, especially the interplay with the 10-round cap test (chained cap test) and the steer cadence test.

Key scenario analysis for `_headlessDrainRound` with the new code:

The `roundCapEnded` computation: after the loop, if `_headlessDrainAction` still returns `drain`, the cap exhausted. With the fix, when does the loop exhaust all 10 rounds while ceiling still has budget? A round that sleeps remainingCeiling consumes the whole remaining budget → next action is detach, so roundCapEnded false → 'drain ceiling'. Good — the never-settling test passes.

For the chained cap test ('round cap (10 rounds)' for busy rounds): rounds where jobs settle quickly — each round ends on settle, quick successive rounds, ceiling never spent, 10 rounds exhausted → round cap. The fix only changes the sleep when wake ≤ 0 && !steerDue. Could a busy-round scenario hit wake ≤ 0 && !steerDue and now sleep the remaining ceiling instead of instant-waking, changing the chained-cap test's timing? Let's think: the chained cap test — let me look at it to see if any round could produce wake ≤ 0. wake = min(deadline-now, threshold distances). If deadline not passed, wake ≤ 0 only if a threshold distance ≤ 0, i.e., a threshold due → steerDue true (same condition: bucket crossed = elapsed ~/ quietMs > consumed). Hmm — actually is that exactly the same? wakeIn computes `due = startedAt + quietMs * (consumed+1)`; d = due - now ≤ 0 ⟺ now ≥ startedAt + quietMs*(consumed+1) ⟺ elapsedMs ≥ quietMs*(consumed+1) ⟺ elapsedMs ~/ quietMs ≥ consumed+1 ⟺ elapsedMs ~/ quietMs > consumed. Yes — identical condition (modulo ms truncation: elapsedMs uses inMilliseconds truncation; due uses Duration arithmetic — equivalent for integer ms). So wake ≤ 0 from a threshold ⟺ steerDue true. wake ≤ 0 can also come from deadline-now ≤ 0 with all thresholds positive. In that case, if deadline passed, next `_headlessDrainAction` detaches. But wait: if deadline passed but there are active jobs... action = detach (ceiling spent). So the round that sleeps remainingCeiling (negative → instant) is followed by detach. One extra instant round, fine.

But subtle: deadline-now ≤ 0 AND a threshold due → steerDue true → instant wake, steer consumes, next round detach. Fine.

Another subtlety: `_headlessSteerDue` uses `_waitingClock()` fresh, while `now` was read just before; the diff between the two reads could flip steerDue relative to wakeIn's `now`. Under a fake clock that advances only on sleeps, both reads return the same value. Real clock: microsecond differences, negligible. OK.

Important remaining check: `steerDue` computed BEFORE the sleep, but the sleep is now the remainingCeiling (long). Suppose wake ≤ 0 because of deadline overshoot mid-drain (a previous round's reaction run overslept past deadline), steerDue false → sleep remainingCeiling (negative) → instant. OK.

Now, one more scenario: wake > 0 but steerDue true — can that happen? steerDue true means some threshold due (elapsed > quietMs*(consumed+1)) → that job's due distance ≤ 0 → wake ≤ 0. So steerDue true ⟹ wake ≤ 0 (given the same clock and same active list). So the branch `wake > Duration.zero || steerDue` — when wake > 0, steerDue is necessarily false; when steerDue true, wake ≤ 0. The `steerDue` in the condition handles the wake ≤ 0 case. Consistent — the pure function's three tests cover the reachable combos (well, the `wake positive + steerDue true` combo is unreachable but returns wake — harmless).

So correctness looks solid. The logic is sound; the flake fix is real.

Now findings to report:

1. **Duplicated crossing logic** between `_headlessSteerDue` (new) and `_steerHeadlessLiveness` (existing): the bucket-crossing computation `elapsedMs ~/ quietMs > (consumedBucket[job.id] ?? 0)` plus the running/notifyOnSettle filter is written twice. The doc comment says "the same crossing check [_steerHeadlessLiveness] applies" — but nothing enforces it; a future change to one (e.g., the multi-bucket burst handling added in the steer) could silently diverge, reintroducing the spin. Suggest extracting a shared private predicate, e.g. `_headlessCrossedBucket(job, liveness)`. Severity: SUGGESTION (leaning IMPORTANT?). Per verdict rules: IMPORTANT = "real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped". The duplication is small (6 lines) and cross-referenced in docs. I'll call it SUGGESTION... Actually the exhaustiveness instruction says surface maximum findings. This is a genuine duplication with divergence risk that the PR itself acknowledges. I'll mark IMPORTANT? Hmm. The repo style is heavily documented; the doc comments explicitly link the two. The risk is real but low. I'll go with SUGGESTION to keep the verdict APPROVE (no blocking anyway — either way verdict is APPROVE since no blocking). Let me be honest: it's a small duplication; SUGGESTION.

2. **Double clock read**: `now` is read at line 245 for `wakeIn` and `remainingCeiling`, but `_headlessSteerDue` reads `_waitingClock()` again internally. Passing `now` as a parameter would keep a single time base and make the predicate pure-ish. SUGGESTION. Inline-able on the diff line of the `_waitingSleep(headlessDrainRoundSleep(...))` block or the `_headlessSteerDue` definition.

3. **Missing integration/wiring test**: the pure function is unit-tested, but nothing exercises the wiring (`_headlessSteerDue` result actually feeding `headlessDrainRoundSleep` in `_headlessDrainRound`). A regression in the wiring (e.g., passing the wrong list or forgetting the argument) would not be caught by any test — the flake would silently persist. An IT with a fake waiting clock where a job sits past the first quiet threshold... Actually constructing a non-positive wake in a test requires the fake clock to overshoot — the drain ITs use a fake clock (`_waitingClock`). Can a test force wake ≤ 0? E.g., quietMs small and advance clock past a threshold before drain starts. Possible: set shellJobQuietMs to 1ms and make the job start long before the drain... The job startedAt is real DateTime.now() per headlessLivenessElapsedText doc. Hmm, the test could use quietMs=1 and drainMs large; elapsed real ms large → first threshold due at 1ms → wake ≤ 0 quickly... but then steerDue also true. To hit the !steerDue branch you need a consumed crossing and elapsed < next threshold while deadline passed — e.g., drainMs small (60ms) and quietMs large: wake = min(60ms, big) = positive. Negative wake needs deadline overshoot: a reaction run that oversleeps. Hard to construct deterministically but possible with the fake clock by advancing during a reaction run. This is a fair IMPORTANT? It's test-coverage debt on a flake fix whose entire value is the wiring. I'd rate IMPORTANT (test coverage dimension). Verdict stays APPROVE.

4. AC5 test: `env.forcedIds = ['sh-1-aaaa']` — solid. One nit: the forced id 'sh-1-aaaa' is 9 chars, same as real minted ids? Real ids: 'sh-<n>-<micros><rand>' e.g. 'sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz'. The near-miss construction takes substring(0, len-2)+'zz' = 'sh-1-aazz'. Resolution: does the near-miss resolver accept 'sh-1-aazz' → 'sh-1-aaaa'? The resolution is presumably prefix/same-n based, not length-based — AC1 tests used the same construction and resolve fine. Fine.

But wait — one more check on the AC5 fix: `env.forcedIds` list is shared per-test env created in setUp, one start in this test — fine. But do later tests in the same group reuse env? setUp recreates. OK.

5. Comment accuracy: "ends in 'zz' once every ~36^2 starts" — correct for uniform base36.

6. Doc comment in headlessDrainRoundSleep references a specific CI run and date — matches repo style of referencing gh issues; fine.

7. Check the negative-remainingCeiling path: `headlessDrainRoundSleep` returns `remainingCeiling` which may be negative → `Future.delayed(negative)` completes immediately → round spins once → loop re-checks action → detach. Bounded. But the pure function's contract says "sleeps the remaining ceiling" — negative in that case. Harmless; could clamp to Duration.zero for cleanliness. SUGGESTION? Very minor; the unit test even passes…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere

  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). Key scenario analysis for `_headlessDrainRound` with the new code:

The `roundCapEnded` computation: after the loop, if `_headlessDrainAction` still returns `drain`, the cap exhausted. With the fix, when does the loop exhaust all 10 rounds while ceiling still has budget? A round that sleeps remainingCeiling consumes the whole remaining budget → next action is detach, so roundCapEnded false → 'drain ceiling'. Good — the never-settling test passes.

For the chained cap test ('round cap (10 rounds)' for busy rounds): rounds where jobs settle quickly — each round ends on settle, quick successive rounds, ceiling never spent, 10 rounds exhausted → round cap. The fix only changes the sleep when wake ≤ 0 && !steerDue. Could a busy-round scenario hit wake ≤ 0 && !steerDue and now sleep the remaining ceiling instead of instant-waking, changing the chained-cap test's timing? Let's think: the chained cap test — let me look at it to see if any round could produce wake ≤ 0. wake = min(deadline-now, threshold distances). If deadline not passed, wake ≤ 0 only if a threshold distance ≤ 0, i.e., a threshold due → steerDue true (same condition: bucket crossed = elapsed ~/ quietMs > consumed). Hmm — actually is that exactly the same? wakeIn computes `due = startedAt + quietMs * (consumed+1)`; d = due - now ≤ 0 ⟺ now ≥ startedAt + quietMs*(consumed+1) ⟺ elapsedMs ≥ quietMs*(consumed+1) ⟺ elapsedMs ~/ quietMs ≥ consumed+1 ⟺ elapsedMs ~/ quietMs > consumed. Yes — identical condition (modulo ms truncation: elapsedMs uses inMilliseconds truncation; due uses Duration arithmetic — equivalent for integer ms). So wake ≤ 0 from a threshold ⟺ steerDue true. wake ≤ 0 can also come from deadline-now ≤ 0 with all thresholds positive. In that case, if deadline passed, next `_headlessDrainAction` detaches. But wait: if deadline passed but there are active jobs... action = detach (ceiling spent). So the round that sleeps remainingCeiling (negative → instant) is followed by detach. One extra instant round, fine.

But subtle: deadline-now ≤ 0 AND a threshold due → steerDue true → instant wake, steer consumes, next round detach. Fine.

Another subtlety: `_headlessSteerDue` uses `_waitingClock()` fresh, while `now` was read just before; the diff between the two reads could flip steerDue relative to wakeIn's `now`. Under a fake clock that advances only on sleeps, both reads return the same value. Real clock: microsecond differences, negligible. OK.

Important remaining check: `steerDue` computed BEFORE the sleep, but the sleep is now the remainingCeiling (long). Suppose wake ≤ 0 because of deadline overshoot mid-drain (a previous round's reaction run overslept past deadline), steerDue false → sleep remainingCeiling (negative) → instant. OK.

Now, one more scenario: wake > 0 but steerDue true — can that happen? steerDue true means some threshold due (elapsed > quietMs*(consumed+1)) → that job's due distance ≤ 0 → wake ≤ 0. So steerDue true ⟹ wake ≤ 0 (given the same clock and same active list). So the branch `wake > Duration.zero || steerDue` — when wake > 0, steerDue is necessarily false; when steerDue true, wake ≤ 0. The `steerDue` in the condition handles the wake ≤ 0 case. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`. The hazard is the loop's own author-documented one (`agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:239-242`: "a zero deadline would wake it at once and spin the round cap"), but only the `0`-kill-switch branch was guarded; the ceiling-sleep branch was not. Both hostile-leg occurrences carry exactly the spin signature: 10 rounds, zero reaction runs, zero steers, job still running, whole test ≤ 90 ms wall.

**Fix:** new pure `headlessDrainRoundSleep` (`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`): a non-positive wake with **no due liveness crossing** (`_headlessSteerDue`, the same crossing check `_steerHeadlessLiveness` applies) sleeps the remaining ceiling instead — a never-settling job always reaches its ceiling and the detach line stays truthful. A due steer keeps the instant wake (the steer fires right after the round, on cadence), and settle-driven rounds are unchanged — the chained cap test's contract (`round cap (10 rounds)` for busy rounds) is preserved. Unit tests for the pure function added in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`.

The CI-side trigger that completes `wakeIn` non-positively on loaded runners (timer/clock scheduling pathology) is not attributable to a single line from the job logs; the fix removes the damage for any trigger: with nothing to consume, a round can no longer complete without wall time.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

The shared box's dart VM is SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137) — attempted ONCE each per lane rules: `dart pub get` (137), `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` (137), `dart test test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart` (137), `dart format` (137, also via `dartaotruntime` 137). No local test run was possible. Static verification instead: 1:1 semantics walkthrough of all four drain tests (settle/error/suppressed/never-settling), the 10-round chained cap test, the kill-switch tests, and the liveness steer cadence against the new code path (contracts preserved; analysis above); AC5 walkthrough against the forced-id near-miss (`sh-1-aazz` vs `sh-1-aaaa` — unique same-`n` → `ShellJobNearMiss` → refusal hint, `stopCalls == 0`). The new pure-function unit tests exercise the guard in CI. `dart format` could not run; the diff is hand-formatted to the touched files' conventions — the CI Static gate is the arbiter.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the

  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files

For the chained cap test ('round cap (10 rounds)' for busy rounds): rounds where jobs settle quickly — each round ends on settle, quick successive rounds, ceiling never spent, 10 rounds exhausted → round cap. If deadline not passed, wake ≤ 0 only if a threshold distance ≤ 0, i.e., a threshold due → steerDue true (same condition: bucket crossed = elapsed ~/ quietMs > consumed). Hmm — actually is that exactly the same? wakeIn computes `due = startedAt + quietMs * (consumed+1)`; d = due - now ≤ 0 ⟺ now ≥ startedAt + quietMs*(consumed+1) ⟺ elapsedMs ≥ quietMs*(consumed+1) ⟺ elapsedMs ~/ quietMs ≥ consumed+1 ⟺ elapsedMs ~/ quietMs > consumed. Yes — identical condition (modulo ms truncation: elapsedMs uses inMilliseconds truncation; due uses Duration arithmetic — equivalent for integer ms). So wake ≤ 0 from a threshold ⟺ steerDue true. wake ≤ 0 can also come from deadline-now ≤ 0 with all thresholds positive. In that case, if deadline passed, next `_headlessDrainAction` detaches. But wait: if deadline passed but there are active jobs... action = detach (ceiling spent). So the round that sleeps remainingCeiling (negative → instant) is followed by detach. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1542
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1542
- **Title**: fix(1539): AC5 near-miss stop determinism + headless drain round sleep never beats the shellJobDrainMs ceiling
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1539-drain-collateral` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +107
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T08:01:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1539

## Red-main evidence (run 38120494810, main 55e4d2851, push 07:10:48Z)

| Family | Job | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| A — behavioral | Core tests (shard 3/4), job 114414103123 | `test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart:381` AC5 `near-miss stop returns a hint and kills nothing` — expected `exact job id`, actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` |
| B — ordering | Hostile ambient env, job 114414103050 | `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465` never-settling job — expected `drain ceiling`, actual `⏳ background-job drain round cap (10 rounds) reached — detaching` |

Family B is a REAL recurring flake, not a one-off: **second occurrence** 15 min later on a different head — run 38121333090 (7790963ed8), Hostile ambient env job 114416566457, same test, same line 465, byte-identical signature (`round cap (10 rounds)`, job never settled, no reaction run, `requests:2`). Freeze-ledger rule (2nd same signature = fix) applies.

Not touched here: the wrap-perf guard reds of the same run (datapoint 3.92x) — owned by #1534.

## Root cause A — test-by-construction collision (1/1296)

`newShellJobId` mints `sh-<n>-<micros><rand>` with a `Random.secure()` 32-bit base36 tail (`lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:61-67`). The AC5 test constructs its near-miss as `entry.id.substring(0, id.length - 2) + 'zz'` — when the minted tail ends in `zz` (P = 1/36² = 1/1296 per start), the "near-miss" **is the exact id**. `stop` on an exact hit rightly succeeds (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:890` → `Stopped $id`); the refusal hint is the near-miss branch (`:906`). The failed run's actual `Stopped sh-1-hn3t16p9ib18keczz` ends in `zz` — exactly this collision. #1463's diff on `shell_jobs.dart`/`builtin_tools_bash.dart` (`git show e294e0434c`) is `markProbed()`/probe-generation only — id resolution was never touched; the suspicion in the issue is disproven, the test was born flaky (gh-1438 shipped it).

**Fix:** force a deterministic id through the file's existing `forcedIds` seam (`['sh-1-aaaa']`), so the constructed near-miss can never equal the real id. Read-only AC1/E4 constructions of the same shape can't flake (both resolution outcomes satisfy their assertions) and are left untouched.

## Root cause B — a no-progress instant round burns the 10-round cap before the ceiling spends

The drain round's ceiling sleep is `_waitingSleep(liveness.wakeIn(...))` = `Future.delayed`. A non-positive duration completes **immediately**, and the loop counts that round anyway. When such a round neither settles a job nor consumes a liveness crossing, it is pure spin: ten of them exhaust the 10-round cap with the wall budget untouched, and `headlessDrainDetachCause` then names `round cap (10 rounds)` for a never-settling job whose documented degradation is the ceiling — breaking the gh-1459 contract pinned at `agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart:465`.
